`RDBConfigStore.UpdateBudgetOverride` loads the row into a local struct and returns before its `Updates()` call, so a rejected override persists nothing. candidate := m.governanceConfig.Budgets[i]

```go
}

```

+// countingStreamCloser models fasthttp's non-idempotent streaming body handle:
+// it implements streamCloserWithError (CloseWithError) and io.Reader, counting
+// closes and reads. The whole point of the atomic-claim fix is that the
+// underlying close runs at most once across the cancellation goroutine, the
+// idle-timeout timer, and ReleaseStreamingResponse — a second close would
+// re-run fasthttp's releaseRequestStream and double-Put the pooled struct.
+type countingStreamCloser struct {
+	closeCount atomic.Int32
+	readCount  atomic.Int32
+}
+
+func (c *countingStreamCloser) Read([]byte) (int, error) {
+	c.readCount.Add(1)
+	return 0, io.EOF
+}
+
+func (c *countingStreamCloser) CloseWithError(error) error {
+	c.closeCount.Add(1)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// TestStreamClose_ExactlyOnceAcrossOwners drives the idle-timeout timer and the
+// cancellation goroutine concurrently against one shared stream + context and
+// asserts the underlying CloseWithError fires exactly once. Before the fix the
+// two owners used a racy Value-then-SetValue guard and could both close, which
+// double-released the pooled fasthttp requestStream and poisoned another
+// request (the `slice bounds out of range [:-680]` crash). Run with -race.
+func TestStreamClose_ExactlyOnceAcrossOwners(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
+		body := &countingStreamCloser{}
+		goCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+		ctx := schemas.NewBifrostContext(goCtx, time.Time{})
+
+		// Tiny idle timeout so the timer races the cancellation.
+		_, cleanup := NewIdleTimeoutReader(body, body, time.Millisecond, ctx)
+		stop := SetupStreamCancellation(ctx, body, getLogger())
+
+		go cancel() // fire cancellation concurrently with the idle timer
+
+		time.Sleep(3 * time.Millisecond) // let both owners attempt to close
+		stop()
+		cleanup()

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed — replaced the fixed `time.Sleep(3ms)` with a bounded poll that waits until `body.closeCount.Load() > 0` (2s deadline) before calling `stop()`/`cleanup()`. The exactly-once assertion is unchanged, so the test is now deterministic under loaded CI while still failing fast if the close never fires. Can you re-check and resolve if it looks good?

Fixed — `testResponsesAccumulator` now takes `testing.TB` and registers `tb.Cleanup(acc.Cleanup)`, so every test and the benchmark clean up the accumulator's ticker/goroutine. All 5 callers updated to pass `t`/`b` and the now-redundant `defer acc.Cleanup()` was removed. Can you re-check and resolve if it looks good?

Good catch — fixed in 4072501.

Added `TestUpdateProvider_PassesThroughForEmptyOrAbsentKeys`, a table-driven test with three sub-cases (omitted, `null`, `[]`) that asserts the keys-guard does NOT fire and execution falls through to the next validator.

Because the handler eventually calls `inMemoryStore.UpdateProviderConfig` (which needs a real `*bifrost.Bifrost` client out of scope for a unit test), I can't run it to a 200. Instead the test bodies set `concurrency: 0`, so the handler short-circuits with a deterministic 400 from the concurrency validator that sits *after* the keys-guard. The invariant under test is: the error message contains `"Concurrency"` and NOT `"keys are not accepted on this endpoint"`. That locks the `len(payload.Keys) > 0` boundary against a refactor to `!= nil` or `json:",omitempty"`.
